source.title: Rubin's conjecture on local units in the anticyclotomic tower at inert primes
source.authors: Ashay A. Burungale, Shinichi Kobayashi and Kazuto Ota
source.version: Published version, 25 PDF pages including JSTOR cover, 24 article pages
readSections: Entire paper, §§1–6, all proofs and all 43 references, printed pp.943–966
Visual formula checks on printed pp.951–953, 956, 961–962: conjugation bars, inverse-character denominator, geometric subgroup and coefficient/rank conventions

baseline.note: No changes to mathematical atlas data, roadmap documents, packets, library coverage or links in the comparison to checked main. Six cited library files matched raw pinned GitHub bytes by SHA-256. No Lean implementation is claimed.

summary: Complete extraction of the published p≥5 unramified-quadratic theorem: integral signed local-unit decomposition from an optimal elliptic unit and an optimal formal-CM local-point system, followed by Rubin interpolation, the integral inert-anticyclotomic CM main conjecture and parity-sensitive CM-rank bounds. Six narrowly scoped library items are reused; ten existing-stage applications are imported; ninety-four missing items have exactly one route. Four Part II directions separate shared Lubin–Tate foundations, local signed units, early/late nonordinary CM analytics and the signed main-conjecture application; one source addition supplies the canonical-character specialization. Referenced proof inputs and the AH class-number/coefficients comparison remain explicit future blueprint obligations, not claims of a closed formalization. Independent review (REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21) accepted the extraction and corrected it in place: route 2's area, several statements (notably Lemma 5.2(ii) at p = 47), locators, notes and supplier citations, and five added items; see research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21.md.

items.name: One-dimensional commutative formal group law
items.statement: A one-dimensional formal group law over a commutative ring: a power series F(X,Y) with F(X,0)=X, F(0,Y)=Y and associativity, together with its commutativity predicate. This is the carrier, not an inverse series, an O-action, a Lubin–Tate endomorphism, a logarithm or a tower.
items.note: Statements read in Mathlib/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Basic.lean at the pin. Reviewer correction: pinned Mathlib's FormalGroup (RingTheory/FormalGroup/Basic.lean:56) and FormalGroup.IsComm (:74) give identity and associativity (add_zero/zero_add derived at :307/:320) but no inverse declaration; the item no longer claims one. The elliptic law has one in Tau Ceti (WeierstrassCurve.formalInverse, FormalGroup/Inverse.lean:108).

items.name: Formal group of a Weierstrass curve
items.statement: For a Weierstrass curve W over a commutative ring, the commutative formal group W.formalGroup, compatible with coefficient homomorphisms.
items.note: The CM O-action and comparison with F are separate missing items.

items.name: Adic points of an elliptic formal group
items.statement: For W over a complete separated uniformly topologized commutative ring with linear topology, and an ideal I defining its adic topology, FormalGroupPoint W I consists of parameters in I and is an additive commutative group under the evaluated formal law.
items.note: No claim that formalPointHom is unconditional: its source has an additional auxiliary-point hypothesis. Generic Lubin–Tate adic points and the elliptic comparison remain separate.

items.name: Teichmüller lift
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field k, the multiplicative lift k×→O× has residue equal to the input and values among the (|k|−1)-st roots of unity.
items.note: This does not supply κ or identify its restriction with ω.

items.name: Algebraic Nakayama lemma
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, an R-module M, submodules N,N′ with N′ finitely generated and ideal I≤Jac(0), N′≤N+I•N′ implies N′≤N.
items.note: The Λ-freeness, augmentation and δ-image hypotheses are proved separately, not obtained from this generic lemma.

items.name: Unramified quadratic local base
items.statement: For p≥5 prime, choose the unramified quadratic extension Φ/Q_p, its integer ring O and uniformizer π=−p; identify its residue field with F_(p²) and its nontrivial base involution.
items.note: The roadmap supplies existence/uniqueness of unramified extensions; the notation π is reused for the modular parametrization only in §5.

items.name: Lubin–Tate formal O-module
items.statement: For Φ/Q_p finite and a uniformizer π, construct a one-dimensional commutative formal O-module F with [π](X)≡πX mod X² and [π](X)≡X^q mod π; construct compatible isomorphisms and its formal logarithm λ normalized by λ′(0)=1. BKO specializes to unramified quadratic Φ and π=−p.
items.note: Supply existence and coordinate-change API, not a record assuming the tower or reciprocity theorem. Generality must also support the existing tower and universal-cover consumers.

items.name: Lubin–Tate torsion tower and character
items.statement: For BKO's F, construct Φ_n=Φ(F[π^(n+1)]) for n≥−1, Φ_∞=∪Φ_n, the free rank-one O-module T_πF=lim F[π^(n+1)] under [π], and the natural isomorphism κ:Gal(Φ_∞/Φ)≃O× from the torsion action.
items.note: Compare κ with the existing class-field reciprocity map with its chosen orientation; do not construct a second local reciprocity theory.

items.name: Tame factor of the Lubin–Tate character
items.statement: Δ=Gal(Φ_0/Φ) identifies with (O/πO)×; κ gives the canonical splitting Gal(Φ_∞/Φ)=Δ×Gal(Φ_∞/Φ_0), and ω=κ|Δ is the Teichmüller lift under that identification.

items.name: Cyclotomic and anticyclotomic local directions
items.statement: The involution of Φ/Q_p decomposes Gal(Φ_∞/Φ_0)=G+⊕G− with each factor Z_p, acting trivially on G+ and by inversion on G−. G+ is the cyclotomic direction; the fixed field of ΔG+ is Ψ_∞, the maximal dihedral pro-p subextension over Q_p inside Φ_∞. Define Θ_n=Φ_n^Δ and Ψ_n=Θ_n^(G+).

items.name: Anticyclotomic character parity
items.statement: An anticyclotomic finite character factors through G−. Its conductor is p^(n+1) if n is the least Φ_n-level through which it factors, and is 1 for the trivial character. Ξ+ comprises even conductor exponents, Ξ− odd ones; in particular 1∈Ξ+.
items.note: Distinguish conductor exponent from order and from the index of Ψ_n; comparison with Agboola–Howard must translate the signs.

items.name: One- and two-variable Iwasawa algebras
items.statement: For BKO's coefficient ring and profinite groups define Λ₂=O[[Gal(Φ_∞/Φ_0)]] and Λ=O[[G−]] as completed group algebras, with continuous actions and augmentation.

items.name: ω-isotypic norm-compatible principal units
items.statement: Let U_n=1+m_(Φ_n). Form Ũ_∞=lim_norm(U_n⊗_(Z_p)O), with its topology and continuous Galois action; let U_∞ be its ω-isotypic summand for Δ. Finite principal-unit carriers are imported; the Lubin–Tate inverse system and its integral actions are new.

items.name: Two-variable local-unit freeness
items.statement: For p≥5 and the unramified quadratic Lubin–Tate tower with π=−p, U_∞ is free of rank two over Λ₂.
items.note: Do not infer freeness merely from the formal inverse-limit definition; Rubin's underlying local-unit theorem is an explicit prerequisite.

items.name: Twisted cyclotomic quotient of local units
items.statement: Choose a topological generator σ of G+. Define V_∞=U_∞/(σ−κ(σ))U_∞ with the induced Λ-action. The ideal and quotient are independent of the chosen topological generator.

items.name: Rank of the anticyclotomic quotient
items.statement: V_∞ is free of rank two over Λ, via specialization of the Λ₂-free local-unit module along σ=κ(σ).

items.name: Inverse Lubin–Tate twist
items.statement: For an O-module with compatible Galois action put M*=Hom_O(T_πF,M)=M⊗(T_πF)^(-1), with diagonal action. Then U_∞*=(Ũ_∞*)^Δ and V_∞*=U_∞*/(σ−1).
items.note: Construct and compare actual maps; a noncanonical rank-one basis is not part of the object.

items.name: Lubin–Tate Coleman power series
items.statement: For a norm-compatible principal-unit sequence u=(u_n) and an O-basis v=(v_n) of T_πF, construct the Coleman series f∈O[[X]]× with f(v_n)=u_n, with uniqueness and the norm-operator characterization needed for compatibility.
items.note: Reviewer correction of the previous note: footnote 2 calls the switch from the p-adic to the π-adic Tate module essential; the (−1)^n is the resulting difference between the generators (p.948: "the generator v_n in [33, §2] differs by (−1)^n from ours"), and Rubin 1987 has sign errors because of it.

items.name: Coates–Wiles logarithmic derivatives
items.statement: For x=u⊗a⊗v^(-1) and its Coleman series f, define δ(x)=a f′(0)/f(0)∈O and δ_n(x)=a f′(v_n)/(λ′(v_n)f(v_n))∈Φ_n.

items.name: Well-definedness and Galois covariance of the derivatives
items.statement: The δ and δ_n formulas are independent of the presentation of x and chosen Tate basis; δ_n(γx)=δ_n(x)^γ. The norm-compatible Coleman identities give the trace relations used to pass to character evaluations.

items.name: Character derivative
items.statement: For χ factoring through Gal(Φ_n/Φ), define δ_χ(x)=π^(-(n+1))∑_γ χ(γ)δ_n(x)^γ. It is independent of sufficiently large n.

items.name: Inverse-character action and anticyclotomic descent
items.statement: δ_χ(x^β)=χ(β)^(-1)δ_χ(x). If χ is anticyclotomic, δ_χ kills (σ−1)U_∞* and therefore descends to V_∞*. Keep the inverse character in the completed-group-ring covariance.

items.name: Signed anticyclotomic local units
items.statement: V_∞*,+=∩_(χ∈Ξ−)ker δ_χ and V_∞*,−=∩_(χ∈Ξ+)ker δ_χ, as Λ-submodules of V_∞*. Unit signs kill the opposite parity.

items.name: Rank-one signed unit modules
items.statement: For the stated p≥5 unramified quadratic tower, each V_∞*,± is Λ-free of rank one.
items.locator: §2, p.949, Rubin Proposition 8.1; Corollary 5.6 and proof of Theorem 5.8
items.note: Separate the earlier rank≤1/intersection calculation from integral freeness and the direct-sum theorem.

items.name: Trivial intersection of signed unit modules
items.statement: V_∞*,+∩V_∞*,−=0, from the character-logarithm decomposition and Kummer annihilator calculation.

items.name: Rubin's local-unit decomposition
items.statement: For every prime p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic and the Lubin–Tate group of parameter −p, V_∞*=V_∞*,+⊕V_∞*,− integrally over Λ=O[[G−]].
items.note: One mathematical theorem, two source locators; not a rational or finite-index assertion.

items.name: Nonvanishing of correct-sign derivatives
items.statement: For ε∈{+,−}, a Λ-generator v of V_∞*,ε satisfies δ_χ(v)≠0 for every χ∈Ξ^ε.
items.note: Includes the trivial character on the plus side with the source's conventions. Reviewer: the proof needs that δ_χ is not identically zero on V_∞* for each anticyclotomic χ (item delta-chi-nonzero), after which the decomposition gives δ_χ(v) ≠ 0 for χ ∈ Ξ^ε.

items.name: Auxiliary imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: For every prime p≥5 there is an imaginary quadratic K in which 2 splits, p is inert, and p∤h_K. The construction uses d from −(m+kp)=dn² with m+kp≡7 mod 8, the class-number bound h(d)≤sqrt(|d|)(2+log|d|)/π, and explicit small-prime cases p≤47.
items.note: A lemma used to produce the optimal unit, not a new class-field theory owner; require checked small-prime witnesses.

items.name: CM Hecke character and elliptic realization
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, p≥5 inert with p∤h_K, and H its Hilbert class field. Let φ have infinity type (1,0) and conductor f, with φ∘N_(H/K) attached to a maximal-CM elliptic curve E/H which is a Gross Q-curve and has good reduction at every prime above p. Then φ((α)) = α for α ∈ K^× ∩ O_K with α ≡ 1 mod f, and φ(ā) = φ̄(a) for ideals a prime to f; construct the rank-one p-adic realization T_φ over a coefficient extension R/O and compare its restriction to G_H with T_πE⊗R.
items.note: CM.4 owns the realization; BKO's canonical-character/root-number specialization is separate. Reviewer: CM.4 plans Hecke characters of CM abelian varieties with their infinity type, conductor and rank-one realizations, but does not state the descent φ∘N_{H/K}=ψ_E for a Gross Q-curve over the Hilbert class field or the relation φ(ā)=φ̄(a). The item is added to route 1 so that CM.4 receives those clauses with the canonical character.

items.name: Canonical Hecke character for the auxiliary field
items.statement: For K chosen by Lemma 3.1, construct the canonical Hecke character φ used by Gross/Rohrlich, with φ(conjugate a)=conjugate φ(a), conductor supported only at primes ramified in K/Q, and a good-p Gross Q-curve realization.
items.locator: §3.0.1 (canonical-character remark), pp.950–951; proof of Theorem 3.4, (3.8), p.953
items.note: Source addition to CM.4, not a second general Hecke-character carrier.

items.name: Root number of the canonical auxiliary character
items.statement: For the canonical φ and the auxiliary K with 2 split, the global root number W(φ)=+1.
items.note: This specialized root-number theorem is not the ordinary Katz/Hsieh branch.

items.name: Auxiliary split-prime anticyclotomic twists
items.statement: Choose a split prime l≥5 with l∤h_K f and p∤(l−1), as in (3.3), and let X_l be the finite-order characters of the anticyclotomic Z_l-extension of K. For ν∈X_l of order l^m use a coefficient ring containing its values.
items.note: Prove existence of such l and translate order versus conductor, rather than assume the admissible set is nonempty.

items.name: Néron-normalized CM period
items.statement: Choose an invariant differential ω smooth at p on E/H and an embedding into C, and a period Ω such that the complex period lattice for ω is Ω O_K. Algebraic L-values and the local differential use these same choices.
items.note: The comparison under scaling ω and Ω is required; this is not an unspecified canonical unit.

items.name: Integral elliptic-unit zeta class
items.statement: For the CM character, coefficient lattice and ideal g divisible by f as in §3, construct the normalized compatible classes z_g in lim_n H¹(K(gp^n),T^(-1)(1)) from Kato's elliptic units, with γ=per_φ(ω)/Ω and the integral normalization used in (3.4).
items.note: General elliptic-unit construction is shared with the pending CMAllPrimeMainConjectures direction from PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26; do not create an independent second construction. This route owns the specific normalized realization and comparison needed here. Neither KatoEulerSystems:L2's modular Siegel-unit classes nor an unreviewed proposed route is counted as an existing supplier.

items.name: CM elliptic-unit explicit reciprocity
items.statement: For a finite character χ at K(gp^n), the χ-weighted sum of the localized dual exponentials of z_g equals Ω^(-1)L_pg(barφ χ,1)·ω, with the tensor factors and embeddings of (3.4). The Hecke character is conjugated, and the Euler factors at pg are omitted.
items.note: Read Kato §§15.8–15.9 including proof. Its infinity-type/dual/Tate convention must be compared explicitly with BKO's; no claim that the modular-form reciprocity stage already supplies this elliptic-unit identity.

items.name: Tower twisting comparison
items.statement: Because T becomes trivial over the torsion tower, the compatible twisting map lim_n H¹(K(gp^n),Z_p(1))⊗T^(-1)→lim_n H¹(K(gp^n),T^(-1)(1)) is the R[[Gal(K(gp∞)/K)]]-isomorphism (3.5), with inverse Galois action tracked.
items.note: General continuous twisting and limit comparisons are imported; verify tower-specific hypotheses at the application. Reviewer: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 builds Iwasawa cohomology for a specified Z_p^d-extension; the tower K(gp^∞) has Galois group Z_p² times a finite group, and the untwisting isomorphism (3.5) itself is not named in L0 or L3, so its hypotheses must be verified at the point of use.

items.name: Disjointness and splitting for the auxiliary projection
items.statement: With M_(n,m)=H(E[p^(n+1)])L_m, l∤h_K gives the disjointness used for the tensor product, and the prime (p) splits completely in the anticyclotomic ring-class layers. Since p∤h_K, the pro-p ray-class direction identifies with the local Z_p² direction.
items.note: A concrete arithmetic comparison, not a consequence of writing two Galois groups with the same rank.

items.name: Localized auxiliary elliptic unit
items.statement: Define ξ_ν by the displayed composite: untwist (3.5), corestrict to M_(n,m), localize at p, split off the L_m group ring, evaluate at ν, project the H/K group ring, project to Δ-invariants, and use Kummer to obtain U_∞*⊗R. Prove this actual composite Galois equivariant.
items.note: Imports the common elliptic-unit object and reciprocity from the analytic direction; owns the anticyclotomic local projection.

items.name: Augmentation derivative of the auxiliary unit
items.statement: For ν∈X_l of order l^m, δ(ξ_ν)=Ω^(-1)L_(l^m f)(barφ ν,1).
items.note: Reviewer correction of the previous note: L_(l^m f) removes only the Euler factors at l and f, so the p-Euler factor is kept here; the finite-character formula (3.6) removes it, which matters only at the trivial character, where δ₁ = (1 + p^(-1))δ accounts for the difference.

items.name: Finite-character derivative of the auxiliary unit
items.statement: For finite χ of Gal(Φ_∞/Φ_0), δ_χ(ξ_ν)=Ω^(-1)L_(l^m p f)(barφ ν χ,1).

items.name: Anticyclotomic root-number parity
items.statement: For ν ∈ X_l and a nontrivial anticyclotomic character χ of conductor p^(n+1): since ν is anticyclotomic, (φ̄ν)(pO_K) = −p (Rubin 1987, Lemma 3.1); f·l^m is stable under complex conjugation and χ has odd order, so χ(f·l^m) = 1; hence W(φ̄νχ) = (−1)^(n+1) W(φ̄ν) = (−1)^(n+1) W(φ̄) = (−1)^(n+1) W(φ), using W(φ̄ν) = W(φ̄) (Greenberg, p.247, as recalled on p.951) and W(φ̄) = W(φ), under §3's self-duality and conductor hypotheses.
items.note: Use conjugation-invariance of f l^m and odd order of χ to prove χ(f l^m)=1; do not apply this nontrivial-character formula at conductor 1 without its own check. Reviewer correction: the inputs φ̄ν(pO_K) = −p, W(φ̄ν) = W(φ̄) and W(φ̄) = W(φ), which link this formula to Proposition 3.3(3), are now in the statement.

items.name: Sign of the projected auxiliary unit
items.statement: If ε=W(φ), the anticyclotomic projection of ξ_ν belongs to V_∞*,ε⊗R, because the L-values at opposite-parity characters vanish by the functional equation.

items.name: Finis's inert-prime unit specialization
items.statement: For the auxiliary canonical φ and split l of §3, all but finitely many ν∈X_l have Ω^(-1)L_f(barφ ν,1) a unit in the integer ring W of a finite extension of Φ containing ν. Prove the omitted-l-factor comparison used to reach δ(ξ_ν)∈W×.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.4, (3.8)–(3.10), pp.953–954; Finis 2006 Theorem 1.1(2)
items.note: Finis's variable p is BKO's split l; Finis's valuation prime ℓ is BKO's inert p. Its μ and b correction terms vanish in this canonical/good-p setting. Read the theorem and hypotheses; full Finis proof remains a prerequisite-paper task. Reviewer: the conductor of φ̄ν is f·l^m (p.953), so L_f(φ̄ν,1) = L_(l^m f)(φ̄ν,1) exactly; the "omitted-l-factor comparison" is an equality with factor 1, not merely a unit.

items.name: Optimal plus local unit
items.statement: There exists ξ*∈V_∞*,+ with δ(ξ*)∈O×. Obtain ξ_ν over W from Finis, use rank-one freeness and scalar-extension descent to show the δ-value of a Λ-generator is an O-unit.

items.name: Formal-group Kummer exact sequence
items.statement: For Θ_n and F, the multiplication-by-π^(n+1) sequence induces 0→F(Θ_n)/π^(n+1)→H¹(Θ_n,F[π^(n+1)])→H¹(Θ_n,F(barΦ))[π^(n+1)]→0, with transition maps compatible with formal traces and corestriction.
items.note: F denotes points in the maximal ideals of the relevant valuation rings; do not confuse all algebraic-closure field elements with formal-group points.

items.name: Hazewinkel's vanishing in the Lubin–Tate tower
items.statement: For BKO's tower and height-two formal group, lim_norm F(Θ_n)=0. Local Tate duality then gives the vanishing of the direct-limit H¹ torsion term in (4.1), and likewise at Ψ_n.
items.note: Only the specialization stated and used here is extracted; the general Hazewinkel norm theorem is a prerequisite source, not silently read or proved.

items.name: Formal points and local units under Kummer duality
items.statement: The Kummer map, vanishing and local reciprocity identify F(Θ_∞)⊗_OΦ/O with H¹(Θ_∞,F[p∞]) and then Hom_O(U_∞,F[p∞]). After twisting, obtain the nondegenerate Galois-compatible pairing with U_∞* into Φ/O, with compact/discrete topologies.
items.note: Import general perfect local Tate duality; prove the actual identifications and topological perfectness needed for Nakayama, not just an abstract nondegenerate pairing.

items.name: Anticyclotomic Kummer pairing
items.statement: Descend the local-unit pairing to F(Ψ_∞)⊗_OΦ/O × V_∞*→Φ/O, with the trace/corestriction and σ−1-quotient comparison; it is nondegenerate with the duality properties used below.

items.name: Character logarithms of formal points
items.statement: For y∈F(Ψ_n) and χ of conductor dividing p^(n+1), put λ_χ(y)=p^(−n)∑_(γ∈Gal(Ψ_n/Φ))χ^(-1)(γ)λ(y)^γ, in a common algebraic closure containing the character values. This is independent of enlarging n.
items.note: The normalizing power is p^n here, not the π^(n+1) of δ_χ.

items.name: Signed formal-point modules
items.statement: A^±={y∈F(Ψ_∞): λ_χ(y)=0 for every χ∈Ξ^±}. Formal-point signs kill the same parity; this differs from V_∞*,±.

items.name: Parity decomposition after division
items.statement: F(Ψ_∞)⊗_OΦ/O = (A+⊗_OΦ/O)+(A−⊗_OΦ/O), with each tensor product interpreted through its natural image.
items.note: The source asserts a sum, not an integral direct sum of A+ and A−.

items.name: Infinite rank of both point signs
items.statement: Each A± has infinite O-rank in the anticyclotomic tower.

items.name: Wiles's explicit Kummer pairing
items.statement: For y∈F(Θ_n), x∈U_∞* and sufficiently large m, ⟨y⊗π^(−n),x⟩=π^(−m−1−n)Tr_(Φ_m/Φ)(δ_m(x)λ(y)) in Φ/O.
items.locator: §4, p.955; Kato 1993 Chapter II Theorem 2.1.7 as cited in §3
items.note: This Lubin–Tate formula is not supplied by the cyclotomic Perrin–Riou interpolation stage; normalizations must agree with the π-adic generator.

items.name: Kummer annihilators of signed formal points
items.statement: The orthogonal complement of A±⊗_OΦ/O inside V_∞* is V_∞*,±. Thus the induced Galois-compatible pairing (A±⊗Φ/O)×(V_∞*/V_∞*,±)→Φ/O is nondegenerate, with the perfect-dual comparison used for compact modules.

items.name: Rank bound from annihilators
items.statement: The point-parity sum and annihilator theorem imply rank_Λ V_∞*,±≤1, separately from integral freeness.

items.name: A rational elliptic curve with a_p=0
items.statement: For every p≥5, choose E/Q with good reduction at p and a_p(E)=0, as used in §5.0.1; the construction may choose the CM examples of conductor 27 or 32 in the exceptional small-prime cases of §5.0.1.
items.note: The existence input is Cox Theorem 14.18; supply actual choices and reduction checks, not an arbitrary E with assumed a_p=0. Reviewer: Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3 plans supersingular ⇔ p | a_q (so a_p=0 for p≥5) and Layer 4 plans good supersingular reduction; the existence of E/Q with a_p(E)=0 is not planned. The conductor-32 case (y²=x(x−u)(x+u), a_p=0 for p≡3 mod 4) is item 69 of PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20, routed there to an Elliptic curves Part II; import it rather than re-proving it.

items.name: Supersingular elliptic formal group as F
items.statement: For E/Q with good reduction at p and a_p(E)=0, identify its formal group over O with BKO's Lubin–Tate group of parameter −p, compatibly with formal logarithms and the selected differential.
items.note: Reviewer: Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1 plans the elliptic formal logarithm and exponential, and Tau Ceti ModularCurves 7E plans that the supersingular formal group has height 2; route 2 should import both (its brief now says so).

items.name: Modular parametrization at the conductor
items.statement: For the auxiliary E/Q, modularity supplies a nonconstant Q-morphism X₀(N)→E with N its conductor, through the modular quotient and Abel–Jacobi construction.
items.note: The optimal/strong-Weil representative and good-prime Manin constant are separated in the next application item.

items.name: Good-prime separability of the parametrization
items.statement: Replace the auxiliary E by the optimal (strong Weil) curve in its Q-isogeny class, retaining good supersingular reduction at p. At p∤N, the optimal parametrization extends over Z_p using the Néron mapping property, and its special-fibre map is separable because the Manin constant is a p-unit.
items.note: Name the good-prime Manin-constant input and Néron-model supplier separately in the blueprint; do not infer special-fibre separability from characteristic zero. Reviewer: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.3 defines Manin constants but explicitly does not assume they equal one; the good-prime p-unit theorem remains unowned, as the route records.

items.name: Scalar Frobenius at the Hasse bound
items.statement: If A/F_(p²) has a_(p²)=±2p, its p²-Frobenius is multiplication by ±p. Every finite subgroup of A(barF_p) is therefore Galois stable and defined over F_(p²).
items.note: Read the bar visually: not an assertion that every geometric torsion point is rational. The finite reduced subgroups here have prime-to-p order. Reviewer: Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3 plans π_q∘π̂_q=[q], π_q+π̂_q=[a_q] and π_q²−[a_q]π_q+[q]=0, and Layer 1 records the scalar example y²=x³−x over F_9 with π_9=[−3]; Lemma 5.1(i) is a short corollary of those, and the Galois-stability consequence is the new part.

items.name: Honda type of a scalar-Frobenius lift
items.statement: For A/F_(p²) as in Lemma 5.1 and an elliptic lift A/O, the associated formal group has Honda type ±X²+p and is Lubin–Tate of parameter ∓p, with corresponding signs.
items.note: Keep the paper's unramified O base; this is not a statement for arbitrary ramified lifts. Import Dieudonné Frobenius from R07.2.

items.name: Ramification bound for the parametrization
items.statement: For the separable special-fibre modular parametrization π:X₀(N)→E and μ=[SL₂(Z):Γ₀(N)]=N∏_(l|N)(1+l^(-1)), the number of ramification points is at most 2g_N−2≤μ/6.
items.note: Riemann–Hurwitz counts ramification with multiplicity; deduce the bound on distinct points. Do not use this for an inseparable map. Reviewer: Riemann–Hurwitz is planned by Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves Layer 7 (the different and the Hurwitz genus formula); only the counting consequence is new.

items.name: Supersingular mass and twist count
items.statement: Write p−1=12m+4δ+6ε with δ,ε∈{0,1}. There are m+δ+ε geometric supersingular j-invariants. Over F_(p²), the number N(t) of isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves with trace t is (p+6−4(−3/p)−3(−1/p))/12 for each t=±2p, 1−(−3/p) for each t=±p, and 1−(−1/p) for t=0.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.2, p.957, Schoof Theorem 4.6
items.note: Count forms/twists over F_(p²), not just geometric j-invariants. This specialized counting input is required for optimal points.

items.name: Nonelliptic supersingular points away from ramification
items.statement: The number of points of X₀(N)(F_(p²)) with trace ±2p and j≠0,1728 is at least μ(⌊(p−1)/12⌋ − 3/2 + (−3/p) + (1/2)(−1/p)). This exceeds the ramification bound μ/6 of Lemma 5.2(i), so an unramified such point exists, when p ≡ 1 mod 12 or p ≥ 31 with p ≠ 47. At p = 47 the displayed bound is μ(3 − 3/2 − 1 − 1/2) = 0, so the printed conclusion "p ≥ 31" does not follow there; p = 47 ≡ 2 mod 3 is covered by Lemma 5.2(iii).
items.note: Reviewer correction (REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21): the printed "in particular ... if p ≡ 1 mod 12 or p ≥ 31" fails at p = 47, the only prime ≥ 31 where the bound does not exceed μ/6 (checked by computation); the paper's final conclusion survives through Lemma 5.2(iii) and Rubin's range p ≤ 1001 (Remark 2.3).

items.name: Exceptional-j supersingular points
items.statement: If p≡2 mod 3 there are at least μ/3 supersingular points with j=0; if p≡3 mod 4 at least μ/2 with j=1728. Together with the preceding bound this yields a trace-±2p supersingular point of X₀(N)(F_(p²)) unramified for π for every p≥5.
items.note: Use the appropriate case, not both congruences as simultaneous requirements.

items.name: Prime-to-p modular level and quotient regularity
items.statement: The prime-to-p Γ₁/Γ₀ modular-curve moduli problems have the finite-étale/quotient-regularity properties used away from j=0,1728, with elliptic stabilizer indices 3 and 2 respectively in characteristic p≥5.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.2 and fine-level passage, pp.957–958
items.note: Upstream ModularCurves 9C supplies quotient-regularity machinery, but the complete prime-to-p j-fibre application with the exceptional stabilizer indices is not identified there as one existing theorem. Route this application only, importing those carriers.

items.name: Primitive formal CM point
items.statement: Choose an unramified supersingular P, compose π with multiplication by #E(F_(p²)) (a p-unit) to send P to 0, add a fine Γ₁(M) level with p-unit deck order, and lift to P′. The completed map at P′ and 0 is an isomorphism; a chosen Q∈Ehat(m)\pEhat(m) lifts to an O-point representing A with Lubin–Tate formal group. Its image P is the required formal CM point.
items.note: For j=0 choose N=27 when p≡2 mod3; for j=1728 choose N=32. Prove this fine-level choice and unramifiedness; formal CM does not imply global CM.

items.name: Deformations of formal O-modules
items.statement: Let A₀ be the integer ring of a nonarchimedean local field with residue k₀, k′/k₀ an extension, and G a one-dimensional commutative formal A₀-module of finite A₀-height n over k′. On Yu's category of complete noetherian local A₀-algebras with the prescribed residue embedding, marked lifts modulo isomorphisms reducing to the identity are represented by W_(A₀)(k′)[[t₁,…,t_(n−1)]]. Fixing a universal lift gives the unique tuple of maximal-ideal parameters for each isomorphism class. In BKO's deformation application A₀=Z_p and n=2; its extra O-action is not a change to height one without a comparison.
items.note: Imports existing formal deformation and p-divisible-group carriers. Higher-height/tower results themselves are not claimed as BKO theorems. Reviewer: Tau Ceti ModularCurves 7D/7F/8C cover only the elliptic, height-2 case over an algebraically closed residue field; Yu's general formal A₀-module deformation space is not planned anywhere, which is why route 2 owns it.

items.name: Formal CM lattice and quotient isogeny
items.statement: For a formal CM elliptic A/O, let T=T_pA be O-free of rank one and V=T⊗_OΦ. For a Z_p-lattice T⊂T′⊂V of finite index put C=T′/T⊂A[p∞], take its Galois-stability field Ψ′, and form A/C over its integer ring using the existing finite-flat quotient theory.
items.note: Prove that the quotient extends over the valuation ring; import ModularCurves 2B and finite-flat closure rather than invent another quotient carrier.

items.name: Quasi-canonical lift of conductor p^s
items.statement: For t an O-basis of T and s≥1, put T_s=p^(−s)Z_p t+T and let A_s be the lattice quotient. Its formal endomorphism ring is Z_p+p^sO. The s=0 object is the original canonical formal CM lift A.
items.note: Define the marked lift and comparison under changing t, not just a curve possessing an abstract ring isomorphism.

items.name: Field of definition of the quasi-canonical lift
items.statement: For s≥1, the minimal local ring-class field Ψ′_s has Gal(Ψ′_s/Φ)≃(O/p^sO)×/(Z/p^sZ)× and degree p^(s−1)(p+1). The non-algebraically-closed residue-field case is needed.
items.note: The degree formula is not asserted at s=0.

items.name: Local ring-class tower and its tame trace
items.statement: Gal(Ψ′_∞/Φ)≃Z_p×Z/(p+1)Z, with torsion subgroup Δ′ of order p+1. Its pro-p subfield is Ψ_∞, and Ψ_s is the Δ′-fixed field at Ψ′_(s+1).
items.note: Compare this field identification to the earlier fixed-field definition, not merely the abstract Galois group. Reviewer: the trace relation needs the field facts Ψ′_s ∩ Ψ_s = Ψ_(s−1) and Ψ′_s·Ψ_s = Ψ′_(s+1), which give Tr_(Ψ′_(s+1)/Ψ_s) x_s = y_(s−1).

items.name: Modular images of quasi-canonical lifts
items.statement: Transport the prime-to-p level structure of A along A→A_s to get z_s∈X₀(N)(O_(Ψ′_s)), and put x_s=π(z_s); identify its reduction and formal-group parameter.

items.name: Optimal system of local points
items.statement: Define y_s=∑_(σ∈Δ′)σx_(s+1)∈Ehat(m_(Ψ_s)) and y=(p+1)Q∈Ehat(m). All sums are in the elliptic formal group.

items.name: Primitivity of the base point
items.statement: The point y=(p+1)Q lies in Ehat(m)\pEhat(m), because p+1 is an O-unit and Q was chosen primitive.

items.name: Hecke relation on the quasi-canonical isogeny tree
items.statement: For s ≥ 1, the p index-p superlattices of T_s of forward conductor s+1 and the unique backward homothety class of T_(s−1) give T_p x_s = Σ_(σ ∈ Gal(Ψ′_(s+1)/Ψ′_s)) σx_(s+1) + x_(s−1); at s = 0 there are p+1 forward lattices, permuted by Δ′. Since π∘T_p = a_p(E)·π = 0 on E, applying π gives Σ σ(π x_(s+1)) + π x_(s−1) = 0.
items.note: Compare the geometric Hecke correspondence with its action a_p(E)=0 under π; a lattice count alone does not establish the trace identity. Reviewer: the geometric Hecke correspondence T_p is ModularCurvesPartII R14.1; the lattice-tree identity is new. Reviewer correction: the step π∘T_p = a_p(E)π = 0 is now in the statement; the paper's "permuted by Δ" should read Δ′ and "of the form σx_s" should read σx_(s+1).

items.name: Two-step trace relation
items.statement: For s≥1, Tr_(Ψ_(s+1)/Ψ_s)(y_(s+1))=−y_(s−1), with trace taken in the formal group.
items.note: Reviewer: the trace relation needs the field facts Ψ′_s ∩ Ψ_s = Ψ_(s−1) and Ψ′_s·Ψ_s = Ψ′_(s+1), which give Tr_(Ψ′_(s+1)/Ψ_s) x_s = y_(s−1).

items.name: Initial trace and zero boundary
items.statement: With x₀ = π(z₀) = Q (since z₀ = P) and T_p x₀ = Σ_(σ ∈ Gal(Ψ′₁/Φ)) σx₁: Tr_(Ψ₁/Φ)(y₁) = −y and y₀ = 0.
items.note: Keep these initial equations separate from the s≥1 recurrence. Reviewer correction: the base point identification and the s = 0 Hecke relation are now part of the statement.

items.name: Invariants of the minus divisible point module
items.statement: (A−⊗_OΦ/O)^(G−)=F(Φ)⊗_OΦ/O. Rubin Proposition 7.4 applies to the optimal system because its proof uses the trace/primitivity properties corresponding to Theorem 5.5, not global Heegner origin.
items.note: Rubin's proof is a prerequisite read for the later blueprint; BKO explicitly identifies the replacement hypothesis.

items.name: Free quotient by the minus local units
items.statement: V_∞*/V_∞*,− is a free Λ-module of rank one, using the invariant computation, Kummer duality and Nakayama.

items.name: Free minus kernel
items.statement: V_∞*,− is Λ-free of rank one, since V_∞* has rank two and its quotient is free rank one; retain the integral splitting argument.

items.name: Unit derivative generates the rank-one quotient
items.statement: On U_∞*, δ₁ = (1 − π^(-1))δ = (1 + p^(-1))δ, where δ₁ is the character derivative at the trivial character (item delta-trivial-relation); since the trivial character lies in Ξ⁺, δ vanishes on V_∞*,−, so δ induces δ : V_∞*/V_∞*,− → O, and δ(λv) = aug(λ)δ(v) sends the maximal ideal of Λ into pO. Under V_∞*/V_∞*,− ≃ Λ, an element ξ ∈ V_∞*,+ with δ(ξ) ∈ O× therefore generates that quotient; combined with the trivial intersection this gives the integral direct sum.
items.note: Reviewer correction: the paper writes δ : V*/V*,− → O without stating why δ kills V*,−; the step (via δ₁ = (1 + p^(-1))δ and 1 ∈ Ξ⁺) is now explicit.

items.name: Primitive CM elliptic-unit specialization
items.statement: Under §6 hypotheses (imaginary quadratic K, p≥5 inert, p∤h_K, Gross Q-curve E/H with maximal CM and good reduction above p, period Ω), construct ξ(E,Ω)∈U_∞* with δ(ξ)=L(barφ,1)/Ω and δ_χ(ξ)=L(barφχ,1)/Ω for nontrivial finite χ. Prove its anticyclotomic projection lies in V_∞*,ε, ε=W(φ).
items.note: This is the primitive normalization, distinct from Proposition 3.3's imprimitive auxiliary ν. Share the elliptic-unit construction with the pending CMAllPrimeMainConjectures direction, and prove removal of Euler factors here. Reviewer: the paper states on p.961 that it corrects "a minor sign error in [33, Th. 3.2]"; keep that correction.

items.name: Rubin's anticyclotomic p-adic L-function
items.statement: For a Λ-generator v_ε of V_∞*,ε write ξ(E,Ω)=L_p(φ,Ω,v_ε)·v_ε. This defines L_p∈Λ, and C_∞=Λξ is a free rank-one submodule. Changing v_ε by a Λ-unit changes L_p by its inverse; the principal ideal is unaffected.
items.note: Prove nonzero ξ using the cited elliptic-unit input and nonvanishing; freeness of C_∞ is not formal for a potentially zero ξ.

items.name: Rubin interpolation with inverse-character denominator
items.statement: For nontrivial χ∈Ξ^ε, L_p(χ)=L(barφ barχ,1)/(Ω·δ_(χ^(-1))(v_ε)). The denominator is nonzero by Corollary 2.2. Hence nonvanishing of L_p(χ) is equivalent to nonvanishing of this complex L-value.
items.note: The conjugations and inverse χ were verified from the printed page. Do not substitute ordinary Katz interpolation or extend this displayed nontrivial-character formula to χ=1 without checking the separate δ identity.

items.name: Global anticyclotomic tower and local completion
items.statement: Under p∤h_K and p inert, identify Gal(K_∞/K) with G− and the completion of each finite layer K_n at p with Ψ_n, compatibly with reciprocity and level maps.
items.note: The convention relating a character's conductor exponent to n must be stated explicitly; avoid the loose reuse of K_n in the source's final theorem.

items.name: Discrete CM Galois module
items.statement: Let R be the integer ring of a finite extension of Φ containing the p-adic avatar of φ, let T be its free rank-one R-lattice and put W=T⊗_OΦ/O. At the chosen inert prime, W≃F[π∞]⊗_OR as a local Galois module.
items.note: Use Λ_R=R[[G−]] for the extended module and L_p's scalar extension. A restriction-of-scalars characteristic ideal would instead require a norm; prove the source's coefficient dictionary.

items.name: Finite-layer signed formal points
items.statement: F±(Ψ_n)={y∈F(Ψ_n): λ_χ(y)=0 for all χ∈Ξ± factoring through Gal(Ψ_n/Φ)}. These are the finite-level same-parity kernels underlying A±.
items.note: Provide the finite/infinite comparison as part of the same local-point API, not an independent definition with reversed signs.

items.name: Signed CM local conditions
items.statement: H¹_±(K_(n,p),W) is the image under Kummer of F±(Ψ_n)⊗_O R⊗_(Z_p)Q_p/Z_p, using the local module identification. It is independent of the chosen identification W≃F[π∞]⊗_OR.
items.note: Give the tensor convention explicitly and show that admissible isomorphisms act by units preserving the image.

items.name: Vanishing of the rational local condition away from p
items.statement: For the CM rank-one representation of §6 and a finite place v∤p of K_n, H¹(K_(n,v),T⊗_(Z_p)Q_p)=0. Consequently the usual finite local condition on W is zero at v.
items.note: Not a theorem for arbitrary p-adic representations; verify the CM weight/local invariants in Arnold's statement.

items.name: Signed CM anticyclotomic Selmer groups
items.statement: Define Sel±(K_n,W) as the kernel of H¹(K_n,W)→H¹(K_(n,p),W)/H¹_±(K_(n,p),W) × ∏_(v∤p)H¹(K_(n,v),W). Define X_∞± as the compact Pontryagin dual of colim_n Sel±(K_n,W), with contragredient G− action.
items.note: Import the general Selmer kernel and dual functor; this owner supplies the inert CM signed local conditions and arithmetic hypotheses.

items.name: Agboola–Howard comparison at prime-to-p class number
items.statement: For §6's Gross Q-curve over H and p∤h_K, prove the analogues of Agboola–Howard (4.2) and Theorem 4.3 used by BKO, with conductor-parity signs translated from their order-parity signs, the selected rank-one CM component, periods, primitive Euler factors and coefficient extension.
items.note: Agboola–Howard's E/Q hypothesis implies h_K=1 in their maximal-CM setting; BKO states this generalization needs a similar argument. The blueprint must supply that argument, not treat AH's published theorem as already general.

items.name: Torsion of the opposite-sign Selmer dual
items.statement: For ε=W(φ), X_∞^(−ε) is finitely generated torsion over the coefficient Iwasawa algebra, under the §6 hypotheses and the sign dictionary.
items.locator: §6.0.2, p.962, Agboola–Howard Theorem 3.6 with BKO's extension

items.name: Integral inert-anticyclotomic CM main conjecture
items.statement: Under §6's hypotheses, char_(Λ_R)(X_∞^(−ε))=(L_p(φ,Ω,v_ε)) after the explicitly identified coefficient extension from Λ to Λ_R. For the O-realization this is char_Λ X_∞^(−ε)=(L_p).
items.note: Retain p≥5, good inert reduction, maximal CM/Gross Shimura condition and p∤h_K. This is neither the rational cyclotomic CM theorem of Burungale–Tian nor an all-prime/ramified theorem.

items.name: Elliptic-unit characteristic equality entering the signed proof
items.statement: In Agboola–Howard's E/Q maximal-CM good inert p setting, let S_rel=lim_corestr Sel_rel(D_n,T), X_str the contragredient dual of the strict W-Selmer group, and C the Λ-module generated by the twisted elliptic-unit system. Then char_Λ X_str=char_Λ(S_rel/C). Their proof deduces this from Rubin's two-variable main conjecture. For BKO's larger p∤h_K setting, the separate hypothesis-translation item must establish this same input.
items.locator: §1, p.945; Theorem 6.1 proof, p.962; Agboola–Howard Proposition 3.3(i),(ii) and Theorem 4.2
items.note: This records the required interface rather than claiming the full Rubin 1991 theorem was read. Its exact proof/hypothesis decomposition is a prerequisite-paper task, shared with CMAllPrimeMainConjectures if that proposed owner is accepted. A theorem only after inverting p cannot supply this integral statement.

items.name: Strict Selmer characteristic-ideal comparison
items.statement: Let X_∞^str be the compact dual of the Selmer group with zero local condition at p. The local-condition quotient gives (L_p)=char X_∞^(−ε)⊆char X_∞^str under Theorem 6.1's hypotheses.
items.note: Keep this direction of ideal containment; it supplies a lower bound on ord_χ L_p.

items.name: Strict control and the one-dimensional local correction
items.statement: Assume additionally E is defined over K. For a finite anticyclotomic character χ and a sufficiently large finite layer through which it factors, ord_χ L_p≥dim Sel^str(K_n,V_pE)^χ≥dim Sel(K_n,V_pE)^χ−1, with dimension over the chosen CM coefficient field.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2, p.963; Rubin Euler Systems Proposition 7.3.4
items.note: Finite control errors disappear only after the appropriate rationalization/isotypic projection; prove the local codimension≤1 in CM rank, not rational rank two.

items.name: Correct-parity signed control
items.statement: If χ∈Ξ^ε, signed control identifies the relevant specialization up to finite errors and gives ord_χ L_p≥dim Sel^(−ε)(K_n,V_pE)^χ=dim Sel(K_n,V_pE)^χ.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.2, p.963; AH Theorem 5.2 and Proposition 5.3
items.note: State the actual finite-kernel control comparison and sign dictionary, not an exact integral equality of finite-level modules.

items.name: Mordell–Weil injection into Selmer
items.statement: For E/K as in Theorem 6.2, the global Kummer map gives rank_CM E(K_n)^χ≤dim_CM Sel(K_n,V_pE)^χ after choosing the CM coefficient embedding.
items.note: Upstream EllipticCurves Layer 7 owns the finite Kummer/Selmer injection; the continuous-limit comparison is imported, not re-planned as a second Selmer carrier. Reviewer: "rank_CM"/"dim_CM" is the extraction's reading of the paper's "rank"/"dim"; it fits the +1 in the bounds but is an interpretation, not the printed wording.

items.name: Rank bound at correct-parity characters
items.statement: Under §6 hypotheses and E defined over K, for χ∈Ξ^ε, rank_CM E(K_n)^χ≤dim_CM Sel(K_n,V_pE)^χ≤ord_χ L_p, at a finite layer through which χ factors.
items.note: Fix the conductor-to-layer dictionary rather than interpreting the two uses of n literally. Do not assert equality or a full p-adic BSD formula. Reviewer: "rank_CM"/"dim_CM" is the extraction's reading of the paper's "rank"/"dim"; it fits the +1 in the bounds but is an interpretation, not the printed wording.

items.name: Rank bound at opposite-parity characters
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, for χ∈Ξ^(−ε), rank_CM E(K_n)^χ≤dim_CM Sel(K_n,V_pE)^χ≤ord_χ L_p+1.
items.note: The +1 is the CM-component local correction, not a bound for the full Q_p-dimension. Reviewer: "rank_CM"/"dim_CM" is the extraction's reading of the paper's "rank"/"dim"; it fits the +1 in the bounds but is an interpretation, not the printed wording.

items.name: Continuous cohomology limit and descent comparisons
items.statement: On the existing continuous-cohomology carrier, prove the compact/discrete coefficient comparisons, full Hochschild–Serre and compatible passage to inverse/direct limits used in §§3–6, with the requisite Mittag–Leffler and derived-limit hypotheses. Reuse existing low-degree restriction, corestriction, cup products and Shapiro maps.
items.note: The carrier is a separate library item. The reviewed audit records low-degree maps as built; only the missing general limit/descent comparisons are planned here.

items.name: Local Tate duality
items.statement: Perfect local invariant/Tate pairings for the finite local Galois modules and their compatible compact/discrete limits, under the hypotheses of the local duality theorem, identify the formal Kummer cokernel with the dual norm limit.
items.note: ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 owns the finite local perfect pairing; ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1 supplies compact/discrete limit comparisons. Do not reassign local duality to the downstream global Poitou–Tate theorem.

items.name: Characteristic ideals and specialization order
items.statement: For a finitely generated torsion module over the regular one-variable coefficient Iwasawa algebra define the characteristic ideal using height-one lengths; compare its generator's vanishing order at a finite character and coefficient extension.
items.note: Generic algebra is planned, the arithmetic control formulas are not automatically supplied.

items.name: Finite-flat and p-divisible-group foundations
items.statement: Construct the compatible finite-flat kernels and quotients, p-divisible-group Tate module, and Dieudonné Frobenius/Verschiebung classification needed for formal CM lifts and Lemma 5.1.
items.note: Reuse upstream ModularCurves 0B/0C/2B/7E at their stated scope. No reviewed integrated audit row for this roadmap was present; checked both full pinned source trees directly.

items.name: Continuous cohomology carrier
items.statement: For a continuous linear topological representation A of a topological group G, continuousCohomology n A is the nth homology object of the homogeneous continuous-cochain complex in topological modules.
items.note: Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Basic.lean:131; this generic carrier does not provide the required arithmetic limit or exact-sequence comparisons.

items.name: Ranks in the elliptic-unit descent input
items.statement: In Agboola–Howard's E/Q maximal-CM good inert p setting, S_rel is torsion-free of Λ-rank one, X_str is Λ-torsion, and X_rel has Λ-rank one. These are the rank statements needed before their characteristic-ideal argument; the extension to BKO's prime-to-p class-number case is a separate task.
items.locator: Agboola–Howard Proposition 3.3(i), as used by BKO Theorem 6.1

items.name: Relaxed torsion and strict characteristic ideals
items.statement: In the same CM setting, char_Λ((X_rel)_(Λ-tor))=char_Λ X_str, with the comparison deduced by two-variable specialization and the coprimality of the specialized cyclotomic parameter with the torsion characteristic divisor.
items.locator: Agboola–Howard Theorem 4.1, used in (4.2) and BKO Theorem 6.1

items.name: Global duality sequence for the signed local condition
items.statement: With S_η the compact signed T-Selmer group, S_rel the relaxed compact Selmer group, H¹ the local Iwasawa cohomology and H¹_η its signed submodule, global duality gives 0→S_η→S_rel→H¹/H¹_η→X_η→X_str→0 in the Agboola–Howard sign convention; translate all signs and involutions to BKO before use.
items.locator: Agboola–Howard (3.3), used in Theorems 4.2–4.3 and BKO Theorem 6.1
items.note: This is the specific arithmetic exact sequence; global Poitou–Tate itself remains with its existing owner.

items.name: Nonzero central values on the correct parity
items.statement: For the self-dual CM Hecke character of §6, nontrivial anticyclotomic p-power characters with the correct root-number parity have nonzero central L-value for all but finitely many such characters, as used to prove the elliptic-unit system C nonzero in the Agboola–Howard argument.
items.locator: §6.0.1, freeness of C_∞, p.961; AH Proposition 3.1 and its proof citing Rohrlich 1984
items.note: Separate complex nonvanishing for a general §6 character from Finis's p-unit theorem for the special auxiliary canonical character. Check the exact Gross-Q-curve extension in the AH comparison before closing the blueprint.

items.name: Trivial-character derivative versus δ
items.statement: On U_∞*, δ₁ = (1 − π^(-1))δ = (1 + p^(-1))δ, from Coleman's norm relation Σ_(w ∈ F[π]) g(X[+]w) = π·g([π]X) computed at any level n ≥ 0; and δ(λx) = aug(λ)·δ(x) for λ ∈ Λ.
items.locator: Implicit in the proof of Theorem 5.8, p.960, and in (3.6)–(3.7), p.953
items.note: Added by the independent review (REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21). Needed for δ to be defined on V*/V*,− and to compare (3.6) at χ = 1 with (3.7); it also shows the "independent of n" claim on p.949 holds only for n ≥ 0 at the trivial character.

items.name: The CM formal group is Lubin–Tate with parameter −p
items.statement: For φ and E as in §3 and §6, φ(pO_K) = −p, and (φ̄ν)(pO_K) = −p for anticyclotomic ν (Rubin 1987, Lemma 3.1). Hence the formal group Ê over O is Lubin–Tate with parameter −p and can be identified with F so that the invariant differentials correspond to ω; in particular W ≅ F[π^∞] ⊗ R.
items.locator: p.953 ("we identify F with the formal group Ê ..."); pp.961–962
items.note: Added by the independent review (REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21). Used for the identification underlying (3.4)–(3.6) and for W ≅ F[π^∞] ⊗ R in §6; the existing elliptic-lt-comparison item covers only §5's curve over Q with a_p = 0.

items.name: Wiles's explicit reciprocity in dual-exponential form
items.statement: For x ∈ U_∞* ⊗ R matched to Kummer classes, and a finite character χ of Gal(Φ_n/Φ), Σ_σ χ(σ)·exp*(loc x^σ) = δ_χ(x)·ω, with the normalisation π^(−(n+1)) of item character-derivative (Kato 1993, Chapter II, Theorem 2.1.7).
items.note: Added by the independent review (REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21). The Kummer-pairing form of §4 (item wiles-pairing) is not the form used on p.953.

items.name: Character derivatives are nonzero on V_∞*
items.statement: For every anticyclotomic character χ, δ_χ is not identically zero on V_∞* (Rubin 1987, Lemma 2.1 and Lemma 10.1).
items.note: Added by the independent review (REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21). External input; with Rubin's decomposition it gives Corollary 2.2.

items.name: Rubin's conjecture for small primes
items.statement: Rubin proved the local-unit decomposition for 5 ≤ p ≤ 1001 with p ≢ 1 mod 12 (Rubin 1987, p.418).
items.note: Added by the independent review (REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21). Recalled result, used only as a shortcut in Remark 5.3; the proof of Theorem 5.8 does not need it once Lemma 5.2(iii) covers the remaining primes.

prerequisites.citation: Rubin, Local units, elliptic units, Heegner points and elliptic curves, Invent. Math. 88 (1987), 405–422
prerequisites.why: The local-unit freeness, signed rank-one modules, Kummer pairing, invariant computation (Proposition 7.4 from 6.1), decomposition criterion and derivative nonvanishing are indispensable. BKO's π-adic signs supersede the older conventions. Full source not acquired; the extraction uses BKO's explicit restatements and identifies exactly where the later blueprint must read the proof.

prerequisites.citation: Lubin–Tate, Formal complex multiplication in local fields; Formal moduli for one-parameter formal Lie groups
prerequisites.why: Lubin–Tate formal modules, torsion character, local tower and universal deformation. Yu §2 states the deformation input; general foundational proof remains to be decomposed, shared with the atlas's tower consumers. The DOI is the local-fields paper; the formal-moduli paper is Bull. Soc. Math. France 94 (1966), 49–59.

prerequisites.citation: Hazewinkel, On norm maps for one dimensional formal groups. III, Duke Math. J. 44 (1977), 305–314
prerequisites.why: BKO §4 uses vanishing of the inverse formal norm limit; the general proof is not supplied by the cyclotomic Coleman roadmap. Not read independently.

prerequisites.citation: Gross, On canonical and quasi-canonical liftings, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), 321–326
prerequisites.why: Formal CM lattice isogenies, endomorphism orders and field of definition; BKO §5.0.2 cites p.325 and Proposition 5.3. Read the complete proof for the foundational blueprint, with Yu's nonclosed-residue comparison.

prerequisites.citation: Yu, On the moduli of quasi-canonical liftings, Compositio Math. 96 (1995), 293–321
prerequisites.why: Read §§0–4 and opening §5, including the universal deformation and Theorem 1 minimal local ring-class field. Needed because BKO's residue field is finite, not algebraically closed. Later valuation/period-map sections are not claimed as read or as BKO endpoints.

prerequisites.citation: Finis, Divisibility of anticyclotomic L-functions and theta functions with complex multiplication, Annals 163 (2006), 767–807
prerequisites.why: Read introduction and Theorem 1.1(2), hypotheses, correction terms and opening §2. Full theta-function/Manin–Mumford proof remains uncovered. The inert valuation-prime specialization is not Hsieh's p-ordinary branch; prove the prime/infinity-type/period dictionary.

prerequisites.citation: Kato, p-adic Hodge theory and values of zeta functions of modular forms, Astérisque 295 (2004), §15
prerequisites.why: The modular Kato roadmap does not automatically supply elliptic-unit classes. Read §§15.8–15.9 including proof for this extraction, supplementing §§15.5–15.6 and §§15.13–15.18 read in the preceding CM paper job. Coordinate the general elliptic-unit foundation with the pending CMAllPrimeMainConjectures proposal.

prerequisites.citation: Kato, Lectures on the approach to Iwasawa theory for Hasse–Weil L-functions via B_dR. I, Chapter II Theorem 2.1.7 (Wiles explicit reciprocity)
prerequisites.why: BKO §3 and §4 use the Lubin–Tate explicit reciprocity law and its trace normalization. The exact BKO formula is extracted; the cited proof is not independently read and must not be replaced by a cyclotomic big-logarithm theorem.

prerequisites.citation: Agboola–Howard, Anticyclotomic Iwasawa theory of CM elliptic curves. II, MRL 12 (2005), 611–621
prerequisites.why: Read the mathematical text through Theorem 5.4 in v2, including Proposition 3.3, (3.3), (4.2), Theorem 4.3 and control proofs. BKO's p∤h_K extension and its opposite conductor-parity convention are separate proof obligations; E/Q in AH has class number one.

prerequisites.citation: Rubin, The “main conjectures” of Iwasawa theory for imaginary quadratic fields, Invent. Math. 103 (1991), 25–68
prerequisites.why: The integral two-variable CM equality used in AH Proposition 3.3(ii) is needed before signed anticyclotomic specialization. Full source not read here. Share its proof owner with the CMAllPrimeMainConjectures proposal; do not use a rational cyclotomic equality as a substitute.

prerequisites.citation: Arnold, Anticyclotomic main conjectures for CM modular forms, J. reine angew. Math. 606 (2007), 41–78
prerequisites.why: BKO invokes Proposition 2.10 for H¹(K_(n,v),V)=0 at v∤p. Its exact CM/local hypotheses and proof must be checked by the blueprint; no arbitrary-representation vanishing is asserted.

prerequisites.citation: Rohrlich, Root numbers of Hecke L-functions of CM fields; Greenberg, On the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Invent. Math. 72 (1983), 241–265
prerequisites.why: Canonical-character sign +1 and the finite anticyclotomic root-number formula in BKO §3 are needed outside the existing ordinary interpolation branch. BKO cites Rohrlich [31] or Yang [41, (5.0)] for the canonical sign and Greenberg p.247 for twists. Prove these specialized formulas and their conductor hypotheses.

prerequisites.citation: Rubin, Euler Systems, Annals of Mathematics Studies 147 (2000), Proposition 7.3.4
prerequisites.why: Strict-Selmer control used in Theorem 6.2. Generic control formalism is planned, but the exact strict CM specialization and its finite corrections need this cited input.

prerequisites.citation: Schoof, Nonsingular plane cubic curves over finite fields, J. Combin. Theory A 46 (1987), 183–211, Theorem 4.6
prerequisites.why: Supersingular F_(p²)-twist counts in Lemma 5.2, beyond a Hasse bound or geometric-j mass formula. The exact displayed specialization is extracted from BKO; the independent counting proof remains a prerequisite.

prerequisites.citation: Cox, Primes of the Form x²+ny² (1989), Theorem 14.18; the optimal-parametrization Manin-constant input
prerequisites.why: BKO §5.0.1 uses existence of E/Q with good a_p=0 reduction and p-indivisibility of the optimal Manin constant. Existing modularity is not a proof of these special inputs. Identify and read their complete proofs before closing the optimal-point blueprint; retain the explicit conductor 27/32 cases.

prerequisites.citation: Rubin, Elliptic curves with complex multiplication and the conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer, Invent. Math. 64 (1981), 455–470
prerequisites.why: The primitive elliptic-unit reciprocity and Shimura-condition normalization invoked by BKO §6.0.1. Shared CM elliptic-unit supplier; not independently read here.

prerequisites.citation: Rohrlich, On L-functions of elliptic curves and anticyclotomic towers, Invent. Math. 75 (1984), 383–408
prerequisites.why: AH Proposition 3.1 explicitly uses this nonvanishing theorem to prove its elliptic-unit system nonzero. The linked AH paper supplies the citation and use, not a claim that Rohrlich's proof was read. This is distinct from Finis's stronger unit statement for the specially chosen canonical character.

prerequisites.citation: Yang, On CM abelian varieties over imaginary quadratic fields, Math. Ann. 329 (2004), 87–117
prerequisites.why: BKO proof of Theorem 3.4 cites (5.0) as an alternative canonical-character root-number source. The Gross Q-curve and sign comparison must be supplied by the CM/analytic boundary, without an ordinary-CM assumption.

routes.reason: The canonical-character/Gross Q-curve specialization belongs inside the existing CM character-and-realization layer. Add its conductor and conjugation proof; reuse the general character carrier and do not assign its analytic root-number/unit theorem to an ordinary-CM layer.

routes.title: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: Lubin–Tate formal modules and quasi-canonical lifts
routes.reason: R07.2 covers Dieudonné classification and nilpotent deformation, but not the Lubin–Tate reciprocity tower, formal-module universal deformation, Honda comparison or quasi-canonical ring-class fields. ClassFieldTheory explicitly excludes the Lubin–Tate construction. A shared foundational extension avoids private copies in local units, ET.6a and VB3. [Reviewer, REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21: area corrected from "cohomology", which is not a galaxy id of data/galaxies.json, to "padic" (p-adic Hodge theory and p-adic geometry), the galaxy of its parent's direction.]
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory). Start beyond R07.1/R07.2, using their actual p-divisible groups, Tate modules and Dieudonné Frobenius. Reuse Mathlib FormalGroup and Tau Ceti's elliptic formal law/adic points; add the formal O-action, logarithm, torsion, coordinate change and complete local-field point APIs. Prove the Lubin–Tate existence and character isomorphism, comparing it with Class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory) Layers 5–8, never constructing a rival Artin map. State these foundations for finite extensions of Q_p as required by the existing consumers, and universal formal-module deformations at finite height as in Yu §2. Import upstream Modular curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves) 0B/0C/2B/7D–7F; prove compatibility with their elliptic special cases rather than reconstructing them. Endoscopic transfer (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6a) owns the later two-tower/cohomological realization; Vector bundles and isocrystals (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples) owns the diamond universal-cover calculation. Supply their common formal-module foundation without importing those consumers or their classification theorems.

For BKO specialize to p≥5, unramified quadratic Φ/Q_p and π=−p. Construct Δ, κ, ω, the G± splitting, Θ_n and Ψ_n; prove all fixed-field and generator comparisons. Prove Lemma 5.1(ii)'s Honda-type assertion over the unramified O base and the comparison Ehat≃F for a_p(E)=0. Construct lattice isogenies, marked quasi-canonical lifts with End=Z_p+p^sO, and their minimal fields Ψ′_s, for s≥1, of degree p^(s−1)(p+1), retaining Yu's nonclosed-residue-field case. Prove Gal(Ψ′_∞/Φ)=Z_p×Z/(p+1), identify the tame-fixed subfield with Ψ_∞, and export trace-compatible maps. These are proof tasks, not data fields declaring the desired properties.

For every construction give extensionality, functoriality, base change, coordinate/basis independence and at least three tests. Required tests include height n=1 (zero deformation parameters), s=1 giving degree p+1, s=0 treated separately, and a ramified-base non-example for the unramified Honda shortcut. Read Lubin–Tate, Honda, Gross and Yu completely to decompose the remaining foundational proofs; BKO itself does not prove a general higher-height tower theorem. Import the elliptic formal logarithm and exponential of Elliptic curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves) Layer 1 and the height-2 statement of Modular curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves) 7E for the comparison of an a_p=0 elliptic formal group with the Lubin–Tate group of parameter −p. [Amended by REV-PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21.]

routes.title: Coleman power series, local units, and cyclotomic-unit quotients, Part II: signed anticyclotomic local units
routes.reason: The parent is explicitly cyclotomic. BKO needs the two-variable Lubin–Tate unit module, a twisted anticyclotomic quotient, opposite-parity derivative kernels, formal CM local points and an integral direct-sum theorem, none of which the cyclotomic Coleman or signed Wach-map stages state.
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Coleman power series, local units, and cyclotomic-unit quotients (ColemanPowerSeries). Compare the parent's cyclotomic Coleman construction where applicable, but begin new layers for the Lubin–Tate tower. Import the proposed LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts foundation and Measures and Iwasawa algebras (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1/L4/L5). Keep p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic and π=−p throughout BKO's theorem. Construct Ũ_∞, its ω-part U_∞, prove Λ₂-rank two, form V_∞ at σ=κ(σ) and its inverse Tate twist V_∞*. Use an actual π-adic Tate generator in the Coleman evaluation theorem: the (−1)^n correction relative to Rubin 1987 is essential. Define δ, δ_n and δ_χ with the exact denominators; prove basis independence, level independence, inverse-character covariance and descent. Define V_∞*,± by killing opposite conductor parity, with the trivial character in Ξ+.

Use Class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory) Layer 5 and Arithmetic Galois duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1) for duality and limits. Prove the formal Kummer comparison, the Hazewinkel vanishing application, Wiles's trace formula and the annihilator theorem. Define λ_χ and A±, which kill same parity; prove the divisible-point sum and rank bounds. Import the early CM zeta-class/reciprocity/Finis results from the proposed NonordinaryCMSpecialValues; apply the explicit localization and projections of §3 to construct ξ_ν and obtain Theorem 3.4's ξ* with δ(ξ*) an O-unit. This early input must not depend on Rubin's final p-adic L-function.

For the other half, import Elliptic-curve modularity (EllipticCurveModularity R29.5–R29.6), Modular curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves) and Modular curves, Part II (ModularCurvesPartII R14.5). Prove the auxiliary a_p=0 existence, optimal parametrization/Manin-unit comparison, scalar-Frobenius and supersingular mass calculations, Lemma 5.2's three separate bounds, fine-level lifting including N=27/32, and primitive formal CM point. Do not substitute global Heegner points. Import quasi-canonical lifts, then construct z_s,x_s,y_s and prove Theorem 5.5: y is p-primitive, y_0=0, Tr y_1=−y and Tr_(s+1/s)y_(s+1)=−y_(s−1) for s≥1. Prove Corollary 5.6, the quotient/kernel freeness and Nakayama generation. Endpoint: Theorem 2.1=5.8, V_∞*=V_∞*,+⊕V_∞*,− integrally, followed by Corollary 2.2's nonzero derivatives for every correct-parity character. Export finite-level signed points without redefining them in the Selmer consumer.

Definition APIs/tests must distinguish same versus opposite parity, conductor versus order, p from π, trivial character, generator changes, and the initial trace boundary. Read Rubin 1987, Hazewinkel and Wiles's reciprocity proof before marking the eventual blueprint closed. Neither p=3 nor ramified primes, full noncyclotomic (phi,Gamma)-theory or a purely local optimal-point construction are endpoints here.

routes.title: Ray-class distributions and general automorphic constructions, Part II: nonordinary CM special values and Rubin interpolation
routes.reason: L3's Katz construction and L3h's Hsieh branch require a p-ordinary CM type. Finis's unit theorem at the inert valuation prime and Rubin's local-unit-coordinate p-adic L-function are not those ordinary constructions. Separate early CM special values from the late function so the dependency graph remains acyclic.
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Ray-class distributions and general automorphic constructions (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions). Import its Hecke-character/period interfaces but not an ordinary-CM hypothesis at an inert prime. Complex multiplication and explicit reciprocity (ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4) owns the canonical Hecke character and Gross Q-curve realization; Global number fields (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields) and Class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory) own Hecke carriers and ray-class fields. Import Bloch–Kato maps from p-adic Hodge regulators (PadicHodgeRegulators L1) and continuous tower cohomology from SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0/L3.

Create an EARLY branch independent of Rubin's decomposition. It proves the canonical root number +1 for the auxiliary K with 2 split, existence of l satisfying (3.3), period normalization, integral elliptic-unit zeta classes, Kato Proposition 15.9 in BKO's conjugated-character/dual/Tate convention, disjointness and local splitting for the ξ_ν projection, and the root-number parity formula for nontrivial χ. Prove Finis Theorem 1.1(2)'s specialization (3.9), with the prime-name switch explicit: Finis's tower p is BKO's split l, while Finis's valuation ℓ is BKO's inert p. Verify μ and b vanish using canonical conductor and good reduction, compare the critical-point/infinity-type conventions, and prove the removed l-factor equals 1 (the conductor of φ̄ν is f·l^m). The result is Ω^(-1)L_f(barφν,1)∈W× for all but finitely many ν. Do not use Hsieh's ordinary μ theorem in its place.

A LATE branch imports AnticyclotomicLocalUnits' completed decomposition and Corollary 2.2. Construct the primitive ξ(E,Ω), C_∞ and L_p by ξ=L_p v_ε, not by assuming interpolating values determine an integral function. Its exact endpoint for nontrivial χ∈Ξ^ε is L_p(χ)=L(barφ barχ,1)/(Ω δ_(χ^(-1))(v_ε)). Prove nonzero denominator, nonzero ξ, period/basis-change laws, coefficient extension and primitive/imprimitive comparison. The trivial character is handled separately through δ, not by silently extending the displayed interpolation range. No ordinary Katz carrier, BDP outside-range formula or full p-adic BSD is asserted.

There must be ONE general elliptic-unit foundation. PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26 proposes CMAllPrimeMainConjectures for it, but that direction is pending independent review/design and is not an existing stage. Coordinate before integration: use its accepted early elliptic-unit construction if available, otherwise record a precise shared-supplier request, never duplicate it privately. This route owns BKO's normalized analytic applications. In the stage graph early special values feed the local optimal-unit proof; only the late Rubin-function layer imports the local decomposition. Do not impose a circular dependency between the two complete roadmaps. Each definition gets API, three tests and eventual suggested Lean signatures; include conjugation, inverse-character, Euler-factor and coefficient-extension regression tests.

routes.title: Main conjectures for modular forms and their families, Part II: the inert anticyclotomic CM main conjecture
routes.reason: The parent L6 re-exports ordinary Heegner/BDP, JSW and Eisenstein branches, not this integral Gross-Q-curve CM theorem over the inert anticyclotomic tower. The rational cyclotomic CM equality proposed for Burungale–Tian is also a different target.
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Main conjectures for modular forms and their families (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures). Final endpoint is BKO Theorem 6.1: for p≥5 inert in imaginary quadratic K with p∤h_K and a maximal-CM Gross Q-curve E/H as in §3/§6, with good reduction above p and ε=W(φ), the opposite-sign dual X_∞^(−ε) is finitely generated torsion and its integral characteristic ideal is generated by Rubin's L_p. Carry the coefficient extension explicitly: W=T⊗_OΦ/O has rank-one coefficient ring R, so use Λ_R and the scalar extension of L_p; do not identify a restriction-of-scalars characteristic ideal with the same element instead of its norm.

Import the actual local formal groups and signed points from AnticyclotomicLocalUnits and L_p from NonordinaryCMSpecialValues. Import the upstream general Selmer/Kummer carrier from Elliptic curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves Layer 7), the compact/discrete extensions and control formalism from Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0–L3), global duality from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 and characteristic ideals from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4/L5. Here prove the global/local tower comparison, local W-identification, independence of the signed Kummer image, Arnold's rational away-p vanishing and the specific signed global-to-local kernel. Keep contragredient action and same-parity point convention explicit.

Read Agboola–Howard II through its proofs. Reconstruct the elliptic-unit module C, relaxed/strict modules, Proposition 3.3's ranks and characteristic equality, Theorem 4.1 and the duality exact sequence, and then (4.2)/Theorem 4.3 using Rubin's now-proved decomposition. Prove BKO's extension from AH's E/Q, class-number-one hypotheses to Gross Q-curves with p∤h_K; it is not a free application of AH's printed theorem. The general elliptic-unit/two-variable main-conjecture supplier must be shared with the pending CMAllPrimeMainConjectures direction, with the EXACT integral formulation checked against Rubin 1991; a p-inverted cyclotomic equality is insufficient. Keep the source-access/proof requests open until this is done.

For Theorem 6.2 additionally assume E is defined over K. Prove strict characteristic containment, strict control with CM local codimension one, and correct-parity signed control. Obtain rank_CM E(K_n)^χ≤dim_CM Sel(K_n,V_pE)^χ≤ord_χ L_p for χ∈Ξ^ε, and the bound ord_χ L_p+1 for χ∈Ξ^(−ε). Specify a finite level through which χ factors and prove the conductor-to-layer dictionary. Dimensions are of the rank-one CM coefficient component, not full Q_p-dimensions. Include tests for the trivial character, both parity cases, coefficient extension, involution and finite control errors. This is not equality in p-adic BSD, a BDP formula, the announced epsilon conjecture, or an extension to p=3 or ramified primes.
